AGENTS.md — ordered

Source: AGENTS.md

An R package providing ordinal classification engines for the tidymodels ecosystem.

Versions

  • Focus primarily on the development version of {ordered} in the current directory (regardless of the current Git branch), not the installed version.
  • For other packages, refer primarily to the locally installed version or else to the online development version (if specified in the description or CRAN page).
  • Ignore the pkgdown website; it may reflect an older version of the package without more recent development changes.
  • {parsnip} and {dials} should be loaded from the cloned development repositories at ‘../parsnip’ and ‘../dials’. These may contain un-released changes; prefer them over the CRAN release. Never request access to any other local directories.

Key architecture

  • Standard R package extending {parsnip} with new model engines.
  • Engine registration happens at load time via R/zzz.R → R/*-data.R (make_*() functions) using parsnip::set_model_engine(), parsnip::set_fit(), parsnip::set_pred(), etc.
  • Actual model wrappers are in separate files (R/*-wrapper.R): these adapt the downstream package’s interface to tidymodels conventions.
  • Custom tunable parameters live in R/param-engine-*.R.
  • Internal validation helpers live in R/parsnip-utils.R: check_pred_type(), check_spec_levels(), check_spec_pred_type(), and spec_has_pred_type().

Models and engines

model engine interface fit calls file key
ordinal_reg polr formula MASS::polr directly ordinal_reg-data.R
ordinal_reg vglm formula ordered::VGAM_vglm_wrapper ordinal_reg-data.R / ordinal_reg-VGAM.R
ordinal_reg ordinalNet matrix ordered::ordinalNet_wrapper ordinal_reg-data.R / ordinal_reg-ordinalNet.R
ordinal_reg clm formula ordered::clm_wrapper ordinal_reg-data.R / ordinal_reg-clm.R
ordinal_reg lrm formula rms::lrm directly ordinal_reg-data.R / ordinal_reg-rms.R
ordinal_reg orm formula rms::orm directly ordinal_reg-data.R / ordinal_reg-rms.R
ordinal_reg glmnetcr matrix glmnetcr::glmnetcr directly ordinal_reg-data.R / ordinal_reg-glmnetcr.R
gen_additive_mod vgam formula ordered::VGAM_vgam_wrapper gen_additive_mod-data.R / ordinal_reg-VGAM.R
decision_tree rpartScore formula ordered::rpartScore_wrapper decision_tree-data.R / decision_tree-rpartScore.R
rand_forest ordinalForest data.frame ordered::ordinalForest_wrapper rand_forest-data.R / rand_forest-ordinalForest.R
rand_forest orf data.frame ordered::orf_wrapper rand_forest-data.R / rand_forest-orf.R

For idiosyncratic argument handling, append the fit wrapper’s argument-value translation logic (matching standardized dials values to native values) in R/*-wrapper.R through helpers like match_ordinal_family(), match_ordinal_link_VGAM(), and match_ordinal_link_ordinalNet(), rather than in translate.ordinal_reg() in {parsnip}. Keep only penalty-path construction (e.g. for ordinalNet/glmnetcr) in {parsnip}’s translate.ordinal_reg().

Development commands

# Run all tests
devtools::test()

# Run specific test file
devtools::test(filter = "ordinal_reg-polr")

# Regenerate documentation
roxygen2::roxygenise()

# Full R CMD check
devtools::check()

# Build pkgdown site
pkgdown::build_site()

# Code coverage
covr::package_coverage()

Testing conventions

  • testthat 3rd edition (Config/testthat/edition: 3).
  • Tests use skip_if_not_installed() for Suggests packages (MASS, VGAM, ordinalNet, ordinal, rms, glmnetcr, orf, rpartScore, ordinalForest, QSARdata).
  • Snapshot tests live in tests/testthat/_snaps/ (one per engine).
  • Test helper tests/testthat/helper-data.R creates shared datasets from MASS::housing (via get_house()) and QSARdata::caco.
  • Test files include test-ordinal_reg-clm.R, test-ordinal_reg-glmnetcr.R, test-ordinal_reg-rms.R, test-rand_forest-orf.R, and test-dials.R.
  • Code in R/*-data.R and R/zzz.R is excluded from coverage via # nocov start/end (runs at load, can’t be test-executed).

Prediction types

model engine predict calls class prob
decision_tree rpartScore predict (S3) ✔ ✖
gen_additive_mod vgam predict (VGAM) ✔ ✔
ordinal_reg polr predict (S3) ✔ ✔
ordinal_reg ordinalNet ordered::predict_ordinalNet_wrapper ✔ ✔
ordinal_reg vglm VGAM::predictvglm (class/prob), predict (VGAM, link) ✔ ✔
ordinal_reg clm predict (S3) ✔ ✔
ordinal_reg lrm ordered::predict_lrm_wrapper ✔ ✔
ordinal_reg orm ordered::predict_lrm_wrapper ✔ ✔
ordinal_reg glmnetcr ordered::predict_glmnetcr_wrapper ✔ ✔
rand_forest ordinalForest predict (S3) ✔ ✔ (only with perffunction = "probability")
rand_forest orf predict (S3) ✔ ✔

Notable quirks

  • ordinalNet penalty interpolation: Supports submodel prediction at arbitrary penalty values via linear interpolation between fitted path points. Uses multi_predict._ordinalNet() and predict._ordinalNet().
  • rpartScore interface: Wrapper converts outcome to integer (as.integer()) before calling rpartScore::rpartScore().
  • VGAM predictvglm dispatch fix: vglm pred functions use predictvglm() (not predict()) to avoid mixed S3/S4 dispatch issues. vgam pred functions use standard predict (from VGAM) — no issue there. See NEWS.md.
  • ordinalForest defaults: num.threads = 1, perffunction = "probability". Prob predictions error unless perffunction is "probability".
  • values_ordinal_link_VGAM: Extends dials::values_ordinal_link with VGAM-specific link functions "foldsqrt", "logc", "gord", "pord", "nbord".
  • Value translation in wrappers: Standardized dials values for link/family/Thresh/parallel_reg are matched to native values inside the vglm/vgam/ordinalNet fit wrappers (via match_ordinal_link_VGAM(), match_ordinal_family(), match_threshold_structure_VGAM(), match_ordinal_link_ordinalNet()) rather than in parsnip::translate.ordinal_reg(). Only penalty-path construction stays in {parsnip}. Native values (e.g. "logitlink", "sratio", "logit") pass through unchanged.
  • glmnetcr penalty interpolation: Supports submodel prediction at arbitrary penalty values via predict_glmnetcr_wrapper(), which interpolates between probability matrices at neighboring path steps.
  • orf interface: Wrapper converts data.frame + factor to numeric matrix X + numeric vector Y before calling orf::orf().
  • predict_lrm_wrapper: The rms package’s predictrms() dispatch does not accept tibble inputs. The wrapper converts tibbles to plain data frames before calling stats::predict().
  • clm prob predictions: The prob prediction pre-processor strips the outcome column from newdata to prevent ordinal::clm from expecting it.
  • values_ordinal_link_clm: Extends dials::values_ordinal_link with clm-specific link functions (see param-engine-clm.R).
  • threshold_structure: A custom dial for ordinal::clm threshold parameter (e.g., "flexible", "symmetric", "equidistant"). Defined in param-engine-clm.R.
  • Encodings vary by engine: traditional for polr/vglm/vgam/clm/lrm/orm/orf, one_hot for ordinalNet/glmnetcr, none for rpartScore/ordinalForest.

CI / PR workflows (GitHub Actions)

  • R-CMD-check.yaml: multi-OS matrix including macOS, Windows, Ubuntu (devel & 2 oldrels).
  • R-CMD-check-no-suggests.yaml: hard-deps only check (catches missing Suggests).
  • test-coverage.yaml: runs covr, uploads to Codecov.
  • pkgdown.yaml: builds site, deploys to gh-pages branch.
  • pr-commands.yaml: /document (roxygenise + commit man/NAMESPACE) and /style (styler).

R package development

This section is taken from the {usethis} package and was written for claude.

Key commands

# To run code
devtools::load_all(); code

# To run all tests
devtools::test()

# To run all tests for files starting with {name}
devtools::test(filter = '^{name}')

# To run all tests for R/{name}.R
devtools::test_active_file('R/{name}.R')

# To run a single test "blah" for R/{name}.R
devtools::test_active_file('R/{name}.R', desc = 'blah')

# To redocument the package
devtools::document()

# To check pkgdown documentation
pkgdown::check_pkgdown()

# To check the package with R CMD check
devtools::check()

You have two options to run R code:

  • Rscript --no-environ -e "code".

    Without --no-environ, every R call fails with "Fatal error: cannot create 'R_TempDir'" because the sandbox blocks reads of ~/.Renviron, which R reads during startup before creating tempdir().

  • If the mcp-repl tool is available, you can use it instead. Note that its default sandbox blocks network requests.

Other commands:

# To format code
air format .

Coding

  • Always run air format . after generating code
  • Use the base pipe operator (|>) not the magrittr pipe (%>%)
  • Don’t use _$x or _$[["x"]] since this package must work on R 4.1.
  • Use \() ... for single-line anonymous functions. For all other cases, use function() {...}
  • Include a space between the bang prefix operators (!, !!, !!!) and their operands.
  • Format code to fit within 80 characters.

Testing

  • Tests for R/{name}.R go in tests/testthat/test-{name}.R.
  • All new code should have an accompanying test.
  • If there are existing tests, place new tests next to similar existing tests.
  • Strive to keep your tests minimal with few comments.
  • Never put code in a test-{name}.R file outside of a test_that() block. Instead, use tests/testthat/helper.R or tests/testthat/helper-{name}.R.
  • Avoid expect_true() and expect_false() in favour of a specific expectation which will give a better failure message. A few expectations in newer releases that you might not know about are expect_all_true(), expect_all_equal(), and expect_r6_class().
  • When testing errors and warnings, don’t use expect_error() or expect_warning(). Instead, use expect_snapshot(error = TRUE) for errors and expect_snapshot() for warnings because these allow the user to review the full text of the output.
  • Avoid the .package argument to local_mocked_bindings(); this modifies the namespace of another package which is not good practice. Instead create a mockable version of the function in the current package. See ?local_mocked_bindings for more details.

Documentation

  • Every user-facing function should be exported and have roxygen2 documentation.
  • Wrap roxygen comments at 80 characters.
  • Internal functions should not have roxygen documentation.
  • Whenever you add a new (non-internal) documentation topic, also add the topic to _pkgdown.yml.
  • Always re-document the package after changing a roxygen2 comment.
  • Use pkgdown::check_pkgdown() to check that all topics are included in the reference index.

NEWS.md

  • Every user-facing change should be given a bullet in NEWS.md.
  • Changes that shouldn’t get a bullet:
    • Small documentation changes.
    • Internal refactorings.
    • Fixes to bugs introduced in the current dev version.
  • Each bullet should briefly describe the change to the end user and mention the related issue in parentheses.
  • A bullet can consist of multiple sentences but should not contain any new lines (i.e. DO NOT line wrap).
  • If the change is related to a function, put the name of the function early in the bullet.
  • Order bullets alphabetically by function name. Put all bullets that don’t mention function names at the beginning.

Writing

  • Use sentence case for headings.
  • Use US English.

Proofreading

If the user asks you to proofread a file, act as an expert proofreader and editor with a deep understanding of clear, engaging, and well-structured writing.

Work paragraph by paragraph, always starting by making a TODO list that includes individual items for each top-level heading.

Fix spelling, grammar, and other minor problems without asking the user. Label any unclear, confusing, or ambiguous sentences with a FIXME comment.

Only report what you have changed.
